Food Safety Inspection | Mandi King 
 Food Safety Officers of CMC conducted an inspection at Mandi King, Manikonda, to assess compliance with food safety and hygiene standards. 
 Good practices observed: 
 • Food handlers wearing uniforms and hairnets. 
 • No stale or expired food items found. 
 • Food items in freezers properly labelled. 
 • No pest activity observed and pest control records were available. 
 Major observations: 
 • Food waste was not being removed regularly. 
 • Cooking oil in deep fryers was found to be dark and greasy. 
 • Water stagnation observed on the kitchen floor. 
 • Exhaust system required thorough cleaning. 
 • Dustbins were kept uncovered. 
 • Medical fitness certificates and water analysis reports were not available. 
 • One freezer was found to be rusted and corroded. 
 • No FoSTaC-trained staff available. 
 • Spices and raw materials were stored in corroded plastic containers. 
 Corrective action taken: 
 • Used cooking oil was discarded during the inspection. 
 • The rusted freezer was removed from the kitchen. 
 • An Improvement Notice is being issued to rectify the identified deficiencies.

 The inspection drive was led by Secunderabad Zonal Commissioner Smt. Mangatayaru. The team comprised Gazetted Food Inspector Laxmi Kanth, Food Safety Officers Swathi and Sahiti, along with the Deputy Commissioner, Assistant Municipal Commissioner and Deputy SWM officials of Kavadiguda Circle.

 ➤ Storage of expired food items

 GHMC reiterated that all hotels and food establishments across Greater Hyderabad must strictly adhere to prescribed food safety and hygiene standards.

As per the instructions of the Commissioner, GHMC, Food Safety Officers are conducting surprise inspections of bakeries in their respective circles. So far, 57 bakeries inspected and 32 samples sent to the State Food Lab, Nacharam and the drive is being continued. 
 FBOs have been directed to maintain hygiene, ensure proper food labeling (prep date & shelf life), and cleanliness in premises. 
 Common violations observed: 
 • FSSAI license not displayed 
 • No “Best Before/Use By” dates 
 • Open dustbins 
 • Housefly infestation 
 • Food waste littered on floor 
 • No health records/water analysis reports 
 • Food handlers without hairnets 
 Notices under the FSS Act, 2006 & Rules, 2011 are being issued. Major violations will face adjudication. 
 #GHMC #Hyderabad #FoodSafety #PublicHealth

GHMC Conducts Surprise Inspections on Non-Compliant Hostels 
 In response to persistent complaints of regulatory non-compliance, GHMC has intensified inspections of private hostels in Ameerpet, Ashok Nagar, and Dilsukhnagar. These establishments, serving students and working professionals, were found violating norms related to food safety (FSSAI), sanitation, fire safety, and urban planning. 
 Key issues include operating without FSSAI and trade licenses, using cellars as kitchens, overcrowding, unhygienic food preparation, and dumping waste in streets. Despite ongoing awareness efforts, many hostels continue to violate essential health and safety standards. 
 To ensure compliance, GHMC formed a Special Task Force to conduct surprise inspections across critical zones. On 23.05.2025, 58 hostels were inspected; 30 notices were issued, 5 hostel kitchens sealed, and penalties totaling ₹2,45,500 imposed under the provisions of the GHMC Act, 1955. 
 Common violations observed during inspections included: 
 • Unclean walls and ceilings 
 • Greasy exhaust systems 
 • Uncovered dustbins 
 • Housefly infestations 
 • Unauthorized kitchens in cellars/parking areas 
 • Food handlers lacking proper hygiene (no hairnets/gloves) 
 • Uneven floors with stagnant water and waste 
 • Cooking and cleaning areas situated too closely 
 • Operation without valid FSSAI and trade licenses 
 • Toilets opening directly into kitchens 
 GHMC will continue strict enforcement to ensure compliance and safeguard public health. 
 #GHMC #FoodSafety #PublicHealth #SafetyStandards
